solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Get ready to fight in fair at university

parts.note: a square deal is a fair one, so square means fair
UP means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: Someone at a university fair is preparing for a punch-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To square up is to adopt a fighting stance, readying oneself for a scrap.

clue.text: Attractively unusual one described by fashion designer

indicators.note: to describe a circle round something is to enclose it, so the designer surrounds one

parts.note: Mary Quant was the British designer who popularised the miniskirt
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fashion designer describes a garment as charmingly odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaint means pleasingly old-fashioned or odd in a charming way.

clue.text: In the morning I depart, leaving friend

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, in the morning
to go is to depart

explanation.surface: A traveller slips off at dawn, leaving a companion behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for a friend, used informally in English too.

clue.text: Short male in abridged Harper Lee novel

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for male is set inside the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the letters take a new order
abridged means shortened, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as the name as written before trimming
taken as written

explanation.surface: A short male character appears in a cut-down Harper Lee novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abridged' cuts Harper to HARPE; 'novel' rearranges HARPELEE, and M goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral means lasting a very short time, fleeting.

clue.text: Sketch left, stuck on beam

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A sketch has been left pinned to a roof beam.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict or describe, as a sketch does.

clue.text: Fifty visiting class mansion, imposing

indicators.note: something visiting a place goes into it, so fifty's letter sits inside the class word

parts.note: a caste is a social class
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people of a certain class are touring an impressive stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a grand, fortified residence, an imposing kind of stately home.

clue.text: Arrive on time to see streaker?

parts.note: to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: Turn up punctually to watch a naked runner at a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: The streaker is not a naked runner but something streaking across the sky; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet streaks across the night sky with a glowing tail, so it is a whimsical streaker.

clue.text: Resign from partnership losing money

parts.note: in cricket a stand is a partnership between two batters
to be down is to have lost money, as in down twenty pounds

explanation.surface: A business partner quits a venture that is losing money.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket stand is the runs two batters add together before one is out.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand down is to withdraw from a post, to resign.

clue.text: Not to mention claw found in shelter

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the claw sits within the shelter word

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, out of the wind
a talon is a bird of prey's claw

explanation.surface: A bird's claw turns up in a shelter, among other things.
explanation.definitionFit: Let alone is an idiom meaning and certainly not, much less.

clue.text: District of capital, heart of Baghdad

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here the middle of Baghdad

explanation.surface: A tour guide describes a district of a capital city at the centre of Baghdad.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is a small administrative or church district.

clue.text: Batter sections surrounding embankments

parts.note: a battering ram batters walls, so batter here is a noun for a ram
parts are sections of a whole

explanation.surface: An army's battering ram attacks sections of the earthworks around a fort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' reads as a verb but is a noun: the thing that batters, a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramparts are defensive walls of earth encircling a castle or town.

clue.text: Elected one-time whistle-blower

parts.note: a party elected to power is in
one-time means former, as in a one-time champion

explanation.surface: A newly elected official was once a whistle-blower.
explanation.definitionFit: An informer passes secret information to the authorities, as a whistle-blower does.

clue.text: Slightly drunk daughter left held by orderly

indicators.note: held by means placed within, so the two letters go inside the word for orderly

parts.note: tidy means orderly or neat

explanation.surface: A tipsy daughter is left in the care of a hospital orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like a hospital attendant but is the adjective, tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddly is informal British for tipsy, mildly intoxicated.

clue.text: Ride, being happy to travel from place to place

parts.note: merry means happy and cheerful

parts.words: to travel from place to place
parts.note: to go round is to visit several places in turn

explanation.surface: Someone describes a cheerful life of constant travel as a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground carousel is a ride whose horses circle a central pole.

clue.text: Star mimed, badly, halfway through

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A singing star was caught lip-syncing poorly in the middle of a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: In midstream means in the middle of an activity, partway through.

clue.text: Without thinking, I slump unsteadily in one

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters go inside the word for one

parts.note: taken as the word one itself, spelt out

indicators.note: unsteadily suggests wobbling about, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Someone collapses wobbling into an armchair without a thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on impulse means acting spontaneously, without reflection.

clue.text: Unexpected exit, perhaps, being cross with role getting sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means read from bottom to top, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix
a part is an actor's role

explanation.surface: An actor is angry that their part is being mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry and 'sent up' as mocked; really cross is a rood.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapdoor in a stage lets a performer vanish suddenly, an example of a surprise way out.

clue.text: Bias in forecast involving the French

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the forecast word encloses the French article

parts.note: a prediction is a forecast
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A weather forecast is accused of a bias towards France.
explanation.definitionFit: A predilection is a liking or preference, a bias in favour of something.

clue.text: Stripped naked during raunchy act in nightclub

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the bare word goes inside the shuffled letters
raunchy means wild and uninhibited, so the letters are shaken about

parts.note: stripped naked means bare

explanation.surface: A striptease performer undresses in a racy nightclub act.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a club offering entertainment while patrons eat and drink.

clue.text: Recalled big slip catch in game

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: a sin is a serious slip or moral lapse
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire remembers a major error by a fielder at slip in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' and 'catch' suggest cricket, where a slip is a fielding position near the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, a game played over a net.

clue.text: Boy has secured trophy? That's right

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the boy word holds the trophy word inside it

parts.note: a son is a boy
pot is slang for a sports trophy or cup

explanation.surface: A proud parent confirms their boy won a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is an informal exclamation meaning exactly correct.

clue.text: When pigs fly in one vertically

indicators.note: in means the letters sit within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: An impossible event, as when a pig takes off straight upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: When pigs fly is an idiom for something that will not happen at all.

clue.text: Avoids extras, permit included

indicators.note: included means taken inside, so the permit word goes within the extras word

parts.note: byes are extras in cricket, runs not scored off the bat
a pass is a permit to enter

explanation.surface: Someone dodges extra fees because a permit is part of the package.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to go round it, avoiding it.

clue.text: Vision of number wanting different leader

indicators.note: wanting a different leader means the first letter of the number is swapped for another

parts.note: eight is a number

explanation.surface: A political party with a new vision needs a fresh leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The replacement letter is not clued; the crossing letters supply it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is the faculty of seeing, vision.

clue.text: Extra extra in addition

parts.note: more means extra, as in more time
over means extra or left over, as in money over

explanation.surface: A newspaper vendor shouts 'Extra, extra!' and adds something more.
explanation.definitionFit: Moreover is a sentence adverb meaning besides or furthermore.

clue.text: Caption, for example, printed in advance

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for example sits within the word for advance

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A caption, perhaps, is printed ahead of a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'printed' links the definition to the wordplay; 'advance' is money lent, not moving forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is the explanatory wording under a picture or map, its caption.

clue.text: Shudder inside Montmartre morgue

indicators.note: inside means the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A grisly thrill in a Paris morgue in the Montmartre district.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a trembling or quiver, a shudder.

clue.text: Paper in stand is last in Japanese

parts.note: to stand someone a drink is to treat them
taken as written

indicators.note: the last in a word is its final letter, here of Japanese

explanation.surface: A Japanese document is on display at an exhibition stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand' is the verb, as in standing a round.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written study, an academic paper.
